pr_title: Allow null key parameters for public keys and certificates.
pr_body:
If an X.509 certificate or PublicKey contained a subject public key info that lacked key parameters entirely, this would be represented as an empty array. A number of places incorrectly handled empty key parameters, and assumed key parameters would always be supplied. This changes the key parameters to be nullable, and return null instead. The places that were incorrectly handling missing parameters now correctly handle "null".

Fixes #110715

issue_context.title: PublicKey.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo() fails when parameters are absent
issue_context.body:
### Description

With post-quantum cryptography, new algorithms are popping up; e.g., XMSS, an asymmetric signing algorithm.

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-lamps-x509-shbs/ defines the SubjectPublicKeyInfo format for this algorithm (registered at IANA with OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.6.34). Paragraph 5.2 specifies: "PARAMS ARE absent". This is allowed, see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.1.1.2.

Note that e.g. RSA specifies PARAMS are NULL (i.e., not absent, but the ASN.1 encoding for NULL).

The example certificate https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-lamps-x509-shbs-13.html#name-xmss-x509-v3-certificate-ex parses fine (e.g., using X509CertificateLoader). The PublicKey property is also accessible, including its raw data. The certificate can also be re-exported with `X509Certificate2.ExportCertificatePem()`, but the public key alone cannot using `X509Certificate2.PublicKey.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()`, which gives:

```
  Stack Trace: 
    AsnWriter.WriteEncodedValue(ReadOnlySpan`1 value)
    AlgorithmIdentifierAsn.Encode(AsnWriter writer, Asn1Tag tag)
    --- End of inner exception stack trace ---
    AlgorithmIdentifierAsn.Encode(AsnWriter writer, Asn1Tag tag)
    SubjectPublicKeyInfoAsn.Encode(AsnWriter writer, Asn1Tag tag)
    PublicKey.EncodeSubjectPublicKeyInfo()
    PublicKey.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()
```


### Reproduction Steps

Using the PEM certificate from https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-lamps-x509-shbs-13.html#name-xmss-x509-v3-certificate-ex:

```
using var certificate = X509CertificateLoader.LoadCertificate(pem);
_ = certificate.PublicKey.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo();
```

### Expected behavior

A valid ASN.1 DER encoding of the public key is returned.

### Actual behavior

System.Security.Cryptography.CryptographicException: ASN1 corrupted data. ---> System.ArgumentException: The input to WriteEncodedValue must represent a single encoded value with no trailing data. (Parameter 'value')

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

Implement a custom ASN.1 exporter, using the `Oid.Value` and `EncodedKeyValue.RawData` (and parameters must be absent).

### Configuration

.NET 9
Windows 10
x64

### Other information

The code seems to allow for nullable parameters, but instead the parameters are set (incorrectly) to an empty Span: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3aa1ec5bb1f50f0a1bed9cfcac8734f742bcf24b/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Security/Cryptography/Asn1/AlgorithmIdentifierAsn.xml.cs#L35-L45

See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
<!-- Policy app identification https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=PullRequestIssueManagement. -->

Looks like the constructor (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/110715) requires parameter data (not nullable). So the absent parameters from the XMSS SubjectPublicKeyInfo are defaulted to an empty `AsnEncodedData`, which in turns fails to encode again upon export. I think the problem is that the parameters aren't nullable, which they should be according to the "OPTIONAL" in https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280#section-4.1.1.2.

The discussion with some other members of API Review was that if there is "significant" value in returning `null` (vs `Array.Empty<byte>()`), then we should go ahead and let null be null.

Given that we show the full ASN encoding, there's no ambiguity between the two, because "omitted" is empty (or null) and "NULL" is `[0x05, 0x00]` (and `OCTET STRING ""` is `[0x04, 0x00]`), which makes it "minor".  However, in chatting with @vcsjones, he feels that it's "significant" because "using a nullable and a type system did help me uncover more places where we are not handling the empty algorithm identifier parameters correctly".

Given that a) the nullability annotation reflecting the possibility of null helped find bugs, and b) there are basically no direct callers of this API; let's consider it "significant to the few callers" and take the breaking change.

review_comments: Or is this because of the weird thing where they're allowed to come from somewhere else in the certificate?
Yeah. My thought was "let the platform do what the platform is going to do in the absence of correct DSA/DSS parameters"

If _lazyKeyAlgorithmParameters is null, calling CloneByteArray() will throw a NullReferenceException. Replace the call with a null-conditional version (e.g. _lazyKeyAlgorithmParameters?.CloneByteArray()) and return null when appropriate.
```suggestion

```
